intended_object: Take a group G acting on X and a subgroup H of G. The definition is meant to be the canonical bijection X/H ≃ Σ_{ω ∈ X/G} ω/H. It splits the H-orbits on X according to the G-orbit that contains each of them. Inferred from the docstring and the type signature.
explanation:
I checked the body of this definition and of the auxiliary bijection `equivSubgroupOrbitsSetoidComap`, which is defined just above it in the same file. The bijection is built in two steps.

1. Every H-orbit lies inside a single G-orbit (`orbitRel_subgroup_le`). So `Setoid.sigmaQuotientEquivOfLe` identifies X/H with a dependent sum over the G-orbits. In each summand, the H-orbit relation is restricted to the preimage of that G-orbit.
2. For each G-orbit ω, `equivSubgroupOrbitsSetoidComap` identifies that restricted quotient with the H-orbits of H acting on `orbitRel.Quotient.orbit ω`. That auxiliary map sends the class of x to the class of x, so the result is the canonical map.

This is exactly the stated object. The setting is already the natural one: orbit relations need a group action, and H is an arbitrary subgroup. The additive version is generated by `to_additive`. I did not find any other Mathlib declaration that gives this same bijection.
